articles.title: ‘The nipple touch of doom’: what is sad nipple syndrome and what causes it?
articles.summary: People everywhere are searching for the reason behind their sudden bursts of anguish or homesickness. Women: was your autoimmune condition misdiagnosed? Some say it feels like a sudden burst of anguish; others liken it more to homesickness.
body: “I was probably a child when I first noticed: ‘Why does touching my nipple make me sad?’” says the 28-year-old. The sensation seemed to happen at random, and without the words to describe it, she kept it a secret. It wasn’t until college that she worked up the courage to Google it. “I realized I wasn’t crazy,” she says.
There are many others like Sandra (who, for privacy, has asked to use a pseudonym). Breastfeeding mothers, queer lovers and cis men alike have all sought an explanation for this phenomenon.

Sad Nipple Syndrome is often discovered in private. People describe it as a sudden dysphoria (a profound state of unhappiness or uneasiness) that follows nipple stimulation. It is often resolved within a couple of minutes, but can cause confusion and disruption.

I spoke to four people who experience SNS, and each described similar negative feelings. Sandra described it as “dread, a nostalgic sadness or the feeling of a bad memory”. Salma Zaky, a New York-based comedian who has talked about her SNS on stage, says she can “tell if a woman has gone through it – they’ll light up or clap”. Zaky likens it to a mix of homesickness or nostalgia.
points: People everywhere are searching for the reason behind their sudden bursts of anguish or homesickness.
Some say it feels like a sudden burst of anguish; others liken it more to homesickness.

articles.title: They fell in love on The Simpsons and married in real life. Meet the French Homer and Marge
articles.summary: They have brought TV’s most famous cartoon couple to life in France for the last 38 years. Philippe Peythieu and Véronique Augereau tell all about working and living together for so long, still being lovebirds – and rarely arguing.
body: The Simpsons is the biggest cartoon comedy in the world, with suburban couple Homer and Marge at its heart. From their beginnings as high-school sweethearts to the travails of married life, they’re an unbreakable pair. Gag-heavy as it may be, it’s also a series with plenty of sentimental plots, from Homer giving up his beloved Duff beer for a month to prove his love to Marge, to Marge composing a heartfelt poem to a dying Homer (miraculously, he makes it through his sushi-induced food poisoning).

Not even the temptations of a brunch-loving bowling instructor called Jacques or a doughnut-guzzling redhead called Mindy could get between them. Plus, of course, they enjoy the occasional “snuggle” (even on a miniature golf course … ).

Now in its 38th season, The Simpsons has also been a huge hit across the globe, meaning hundreds of international actors have voiced this much-loved couple. Among them are Philippe Peythieu and Véronique Augereau, who – as well as playing Marge and Homer in the French dub of The Simpsons since 1990 – met through the show and ended up getting married.
points: They have brought TV’s most famous cartoon couple to life in France for the last 38 years.

articles.title: I spent 11 years without my childhood friend. Finding our way back together was staggeringly simple
articles.summary: I thought about her a lot after our friendship imploded. When our birthdays rolled around, I wondered what we’d be doing if we were still in touch. I was 26 when I lost my childhood friend. By that point, I’d known her for almost two-thirds of my life.
body: Our first conversation was at an ice-skating party when we were nine years old. I’d been nervous in the weeks leading up to the party because I couldn’t ice-skate. Every time the Spice Girls’ 2 Become 1 music video came on, the sight of Victoria Beckham singing on an ice rink filled me with impending doom. I was sure I would disgrace myself at the party.

But the party – and I don’t often say this about parties – was a blast. As it turned out, my in-line skating experience gave me some advantage on the ice, and I met a girl who was easy to talk to. I was a shy child, so I was struck by that sense of ease – how I wasn’t panicking about what to say or lurking awkwardly on the edge of a conversation. I can’t remember what we talked about. She was kind enough not to mention the fact I’d chosen to wear a dolphin-print sarong. We held hands and at one point she asked: “What’s your name again?” Apparently, we’d had so much to say to each other, we’d skated right over all the usual greetings and pleasantries.

articles.title: Getting to Know New York Through Its Sandwiches
articles.summary: From pho-inspired wraps to a Pakistani-style chopped cheese, a writer tastes the many flavors that shape NYC on a sandwich tour through the East Village.
body: An expert-led tour that starts by questioning its own object of inquiry is unconventional. But then, so is our guide. Ben Gollan, known to his Instagram followers as A Man and His Sandwich, has spent the last nine years reviewing sandwiches across New York City. Gollan moved here from Australia in 2016, after nearly a decade as a government lawyer. For about as long, he has run an Airbnb Experience that turns a food crawl into a two-hour pilgrimage to the city’s best sandwich slingers.

It was a pastrami sandwich at Harry & Ida’s, a former deli in the East Village, that turned Gollan into a professional sandwich hound. “It was a fourth-generation Jewish deli that broke every rule of pastrami sandwiches: it was thick-cut and fabulous,” he says as we dash across Bowery. We’re scuttling over from a coffee shop in Cooper Square that served as our meeting point and into the East Village—a neighborhood of contrasts that still manages to connect New York's past and present. There are 12 of us in total, mostly locals, a couple of newer transplants, and just one traveler. “It’s usually mostly visitors, so this is different,” he says.

articles.title: How Flavored Syrup Became a Coffee-Shop Culture War
articles.summary: In a TikTok video with over 82,000 likes, the person behind the camera zooms into the shelves at a Pennsylvania coffee shop, three rows stacked with an array of Torani syrups in flavors like blueberry, brown-sugar cinnamon, English toffee, and salted caramel.
body: For some coffee shop customers, premade syrups are now a major red flag. It presents a new opportunity for small business owners.

It’s not just a Torani problem, though the brand — by virtue of its market dominance — tends to get the most flack on social media. While some people seem to prefer competitor Monin, it, too, draws backlash over allegations of tasting “like chemicals.” The problem, for some drinkers of dessert-like specialty beverages, is premade syrups across the board.

For a certain sect of consumers, they’ve become a coffee shop red flag, a sign that a so-called “specialty” establishment asking them to fork over $8 plus tip for a latte is unfairly cutting corners when it comes to quality or craft. For these consumers, mass-market syrups now symbolize exactly that: They’re synonymous with coffee chains and corporations, the kind of impersonal institutions that many people are trying to get away from when they patronize a small business. The flip side: For independently owned coffee shops across the country, house-made syrup now represents a major opportunity.

articles.title: At the NYPL’s Library Lions Gala, a Night Celebrating Libraries and Democracy
articles.summary: On the eve of Election Day, the 2026 Library Lions Gala transformed the New York Public Library on Fifth Avenue into a black-tie celebration honoring this year's Lions—Joy Harjo, Stephen King, George Packer, Aaron Sorkin, Martha Stewart, and Jesmyn Ward.
body: There’s just one night of the year when the majestic steps outside the New York Public Library on Fifth Avenue are covered in candles as opposed to tourists; when the metal detectors in Astor Hall are momentarily replaced by cocktail high-tops; when the long oak study tables in the historic Rose Main Reading Room are transformed into tablescapes laden with crimson roses and peonies. It is, of course, the Library Lions gala.

Anthony Marx, president of the New York Public Library, echoed her sentiment. “We are and will remain the source of trustworthy information. All too rare these days, trustworthy information as a public good is the foundation of an informed democracy, which will be relevant tomorrow and the foundation for everyone’s economic opportunity,” he said. “Millions depend on us.”

The program continued with a video featuring all six newly minted Lions, where Sorkin said it best: “I think libraries are one of the fundamental institutions, not just of a literate society but of a democracy. And the less we invest in them, the more we try to use political power to control what’s in them, the weaker our democracy becomes.”

articles.title: Five Creative Ways to Spend Your FSA Funds Before the End of the Year
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. If you have a flexible spending account (FSA), you know the drill: Use the funds before the end of the year, or lose them. Unfortunately, chances are slim you can pack the rest of the year with doctor's appointments.
body: As the end of the year approaches, here are all the ways you can spend any leftover money in your FSA balance.

Many over-the-counter medications and health items are FSA-eligible, including pain relievers, cold medicine, bandages, dental care products, menstrual products, and more. Scan your medicine cabinet and make a list of anything you need to stock up on.

FSA/HSA eligibility for smartwatches and other fitness wearables is real, but the main “catch" (as I’ve previously explained ) is proving the device is in fact necessary, which requires you to obtain a Letter of Medical Necessity (LMN).

Screenless recovery trackers like Whoop, Amazfit Helio Strap, and the Oura Ring can usually be justified as HSA/FSA eligible around sleep quality, HRV-based stress monitoring, or recovery tracking tied to a chronic condition. Similarly, smartwatches can qualify the same way a basic tracker does, as long as you can link a relevant documented health concern. For instance, Coros offers FSA/HSA eligibility for all its watches and heart rate monitors through its partnership with Truemed. Amazfit similarly lets you filter by HSA/FSA eligibility for its smartwatches.

articles.title: Lupita Nyong’o Brought 3 Dresses—and a Bag of Swedish Candy—to the 2026 CFDA Awards
articles.summary: “My off-duty style is relaxed, effortless, and comfortable, but always with a sense of personality. I love pieces that feel easy to wear but still allow me to express myself,” Nyong’o tells 'Vogue.'
body: Never has anyone at the CFDA Awards been this comfortable and stylish. Last night, Lupita Nyong’o celebrated the best of American fashion at the Museum of Natural History with three custom looks for the occasion.

After an afternoon spent getting ready at the Fifth Avenue Hotel, listening to Stevie Wonder and Meshell Ndegeocello while snacking on leftover Swedish candy from Halloween, it was time for Nyong’o to slip on her first of three GapStudio looks by Zac Posen, who was honored last night with the Innovation Award.

For his longtime friend’s fashion triple header, Posen was inspired by the classic Gap T-shirt and—more broadly—American sportswear. “We built the looks on T-shirt jersey, the fabric at the heart of Gap. Easy, understated, comfortable chic,” Posen says. “It’s a classic casual fabric, elevated by the woman who wears it.”

body: PCMag called it a “battery beast” in its review of the Ultra 4, giving it an “Excellent” rating and citing its “jaw-dropping 74-hour battery life” in testing. Apple rates the watch for up to 50 hours of normal use and up to 84 hours in Low Power Mode. The updated Ultra 4 also has a faster S11 chip and precision health tracking, making it a more capable competitor to rugged outdoor watches from brands like Garmin. It’s designed for people who want a durable companion for adventures and endurance workouts.

While the design and display remain largely unchanged, the S11 chip supports new software and health features, including a Readiness Score that assesses the user’s recent activity, sleep, and health data, then offers a daily recommendation. It also has updated heart-rate monitoring and step counting. This model comes with cellular connectivity and dual-frequency GPS. If you’re an Apple user looking for a rugged watch with multi-day battery life and detailed health tracking, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 could suit everyday users and serious adventurers alike.
